A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MASNET research and provide complete, readable main text and appendices. The original technical and experimental appendices can be matched reliably despite v2 inserting a related-work appendix and changing section labels.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix 10 report original set-containment experiments on synthetic, text and point-cloud data, plus monotone-function approximation results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain these original experiments, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and supplementary results.

M1.justification: The MASNET architectures, Hat/ReLU/TRI/INT variants, aggregation, monotone outer mappings and training objectives are unchanged. Appendix 9's model details are retained as Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic containment tasks, MSWEB, MSNBC, Amazon Bedding/Feeding, ModelNet40 and monotone-function approximation. Appendix A's additional application discussion introduces no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain identical comparator membership: DeepSets and Set Transformer, with FlexSubNet and Neural SFE where previously evaluated. Citation renumbering does not change the baselines.

E3.justification: Reported splits, embedding dimensions, losses, metrics, noise levels, class ratios, set sizes and point-cloud encoders are unchanged. The supplementary protocols in Appendix 10 are retained in Appendix D.

E4.justification: The set-size sensitivity plots, shallow-versus-deep comparisons, monotone-outer-network and Hat-scaling ablations, and supplementary noise and class-ratio analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains identical plus/minus uncertainty reporting. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The experimental tables and plots retain identical results, including all supplementary entries. For example, Table 7 reports MASNET-Hat MAE of 0.00959 ± 0.00016 in both versions.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds a brief mathematical formulation of the background set-splitting problem when discussing Blum and Rivest. The paper's MAS definitions, bounds, separability and universality results, and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about MAS functions, embedding-dimension bounds, infinite-domain impossibility, weakly MAS neural models, stability, universality and empirical effectiveness retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of experimental behavior and model choices remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitations concerning post-training guarantees, universality on infinite ground sets and extension to subgraph problems.

D1.justification: Implementation, hardware and data-preparation details are unchanged. Although v2 prints the repository URL explicitly in the abstract, v1's GitHub hyperlink already points to the same repository.

R1.justification: The rewritten introduction and new Appendix A substantially expand explanations connecting MAS to monotone learning, capacities, fuzzy measures, order dimension and injective embeddings. Two works by Agahi and by Czogala–Drewniak are added, while the Agahi–Ouyang citation is removed; most other reference revisions concern metadata.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the introductory related-work paragraphs, new Appendix A and bibliography. Existing appendices change from sections 8–10 to B–D, with corresponding cross-reference and punctuation edits; the core narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: The bibliography is condensed and reflowed, and the appendix opening changes to accommodate Appendix A. Existing figures and tables retain their designs, captions and arrangement within corresponding content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's brief literature overview, the revised introduction and Appendix A provide more explicit context for the relationship to monotonicity, order dimension and injective representations. This offers a limited improvement in positioning. Awkward and incomplete prose in the added appendix limits that benefit, while the original technical results, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
